reviews.one_line_contribution: Segment GEPA-optimized prompts into typed atomic clauses, causally estimate each clause's contribution both on its source task (deletion) and on seven other tasks (insertion) to build a clause x target portability matrix, and use it to claim a dissociation — source contribution does not predict transfer, clause type does — cashed out as a zero-rollout portable-clause library priced in cold-start GEPA rollouts.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Three works threaten different halves. (1) ContextCite (Cohen-Wang et al., 2024) already estimates causal contributions of individual context segments by random ablation plus a linear surrogate over presence indicators — that is Experiment (4b) essentially verbatim; the methodological contribution is therefore a reapplication, not a new estimator, and the proposal never cites it. (2) Battle & Gollapudi, 'The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Eccentric Automatic Prompts' (2024), reports that optimizer-discovered prompt text is idiosyncratic to the task and executor and does not carry over — which is the proposal's Prediction (c) for content clauses already in the literature, and also predicts that the portable residue will be small enough to be swallowed by the filler/sham controls. (3) Bsharat et al., 'Principled Instructions Are All You Need' (2024), is a hand-written, empirically evaluated generic instruction checklist (output contracts, edge-case handling, decomposition) — i.e., Baseline (iii) already exists as a published artifact, so if the harvested library merely matches it the paper reduces to a replication with a negative result. The proposal's stated foils (SPoT/ATTEMPT, OPRO, APE, MIPROv2) are correctly dismissed as monolithic or soft-prompt, but they are the easy foils; the hard ones above are unaddressed.
reviews.strongest_objection: The central dissociation (Prediction b) is confounded by construction, because the two correlated quantities are measured in incomparable regimes. Source contribution comes from Experiment (4): deleting a clause from a fully optimized prompt in which every other optimized clause is still present. Cross-task contribution comes from Experiment (5): inserting that clause into the target's bare baseline prompt. Prompt gains are strongly submodular — a clause deleted from a saturated optimized prompt shows a small marginal effect because its function is redundantly covered, while the same clause dropped into an unoptimized baseline with full headroom shows a large one. A low Spearman correlation between a deletion-from-saturated estimate and an insertion-into-empty estimate is the expected signature of headroom and redundancy asymmetry alone, and would be obtained even if every clause were perfectly domain-general. Attenuation correction does not touch this; it corrects for unreliability, not for a systematic context difference. Worse, the same confound loads the effect onto clause type in the predicted direction for a second, non-empirical reason: output-contract and error-avoidance clauses are exactly the clauses a bare baseline prompt lacks, while task-specific-content clauses are, by the taxonomy's own definition, statements about the source domain, so inserting 'identify the bridge entity linking the two supporting passages' into GSM8K is a straw-man manipulation whose failure is analytic rather than discovered. Predictions (a) and (c) are therefore close to entailed by the seven-way labeling scheme, and a reviewer will say the headline finding is a restatement of the taxonomy. Secondary but also sinking: the title claims 'Prompt Optimizers' while only one optimizer (a GEPA reimplementation) is run, so nothing licenses the plural; and the eight generalization units are not eight domains — two BBH clusters and two Super-NaturalInstructions clusters are format siblings, so leave-one-target-out folds leak suite conventions and will inflate measured portability without a within-suite vs cross-suite split.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Make the two attribution regimes symmetric before correlating them: measure each clause's source contribution by insertion into its own task's baseline prompt (matching Experiment 5's operation exactly), and/or measure cross-task contribution by insertion into the target's own GEPA-optimized prompt, and pre-register Prediction (b) on the matched pair. Report the deletion-vs-insertion gap explicitly as a redundancy measure — it is a real finding and it is the thing currently masquerading as the dissociation. Second, gate the dissociation on the domain-scrubbed condition rather than leaving scrubbing as an ablation: if the effect survives after source-domain nouns are stripped and a leakage probe cannot recover the source task, it is empirical; if it does not, the paper should say the dissociation is definitional. Third, run MIPROv2 or a second optimizer family on at least three tasks, or retitle to a single-optimizer claim. Fourth, fix Prediction (c): '>=15% of content-clause x target cells negative beyond the noise floor' is a selection-on-noise statistic that conflicts with the proposal's own admission that per-cell MDE is ~4 points, so it must be paired with the symmetric count of positive cells beyond the floor and an FDR correction, otherwise both counts will be nonzero by construction. Fifth, split the leave-one-target-out results into within-suite and cross-suite folds. Sixth, actually run the preprint search.
reviews.missing_baseline: An LLM-abstraction baseline with zero causal measurement: hand the reflector model the seven source tasks' final optimized prompts and ask it to write a generic, domain-stripped prefix of matched token length. This is the arm that decides whether the ~336k-generation attribution apparatus earns its cost. Baseline (iii), the hand-written checklist, tests only whether harvesting from optimizer output was necessary; it does not test whether *causal portability estimation* was necessary, and the proposal's own hypothesis — that a cheap type label predicts transfer better than measured source contribution does — implies that cheap label-based or LLM-summarized selection may match the measured library. For the same reason, type-label-only selection (choose all output-contract and error-avoidance clauses, no portability measurement) belongs in the headline comparison in Experiment (7), not buried as a single-type ablation. Also absent: a target-task-agnostic exemplar baseline, i.e. the best source prompt's exemplar clauses alone, which is the arm practitioners would actually try first.
reviews.preprint_collision: Absent, and the omission is disqualifying rather than neutral. The Preprint Collision Check field is empty, and Related Work opens with '(All citations unverified; literature search backend was unavailable.)' — so the submission contains zero evidence that anyone looked for recent work, on a topic where prompt-component ablation, prompt-segment attribution, and reusable generic prompt prefixes are all active arXiv areas. Specific likely collisions the authors must clear: ContextCite-style random-ablation attribution over prompt/context segments (the exact estimator in 4b); the 'eccentric automatic prompts' line showing optimizer-discovered text is task- and model-idiosyncratic (pre-empts Prediction c); published hand-written generic instruction checklists such as the 26-principles work (pre-empts Baseline iii and possibly the whole library); and the growing set of GEPA/MIPRO follow-up preprints on warm-starting and cross-task prompt reuse, at least one of which is likely to have reported instruction-skeleton reuse budget curves. I cannot verify from here which of these has already published the clause x target matrix specifically, and that is precisely the problem: the proposal asks the reviewer to take its novelty on faith. Novelty is scored as not established, not as absent.

reviews.one_line_contribution: Segment GEPA-optimized prompts into atomic clauses, estimate each clause's causal contribution both on its source task and when inserted into seven other tasks' baseline prompts, and use the resulting clause x target portability matrix to build a zero-rollout generic prefix whose value is priced in cold-start GEPA-rollout equivalents.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two lines threaten it. (1) Min et al. 2022 (Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations) and Madaan & Yazdanbakhsh 2022 (Text and Patterns: For Effective Chain of Thought It Takes Two to Tango) already do component-wise counterfactual ablation of prompts and already report the exact dissociation this proposal predicts: the format/contract scaffold carries most of the benefit while the domain content contributes far less than its salience suggests. That is prediction (c) in a different wrapper. The proposal's answer -- 'those were hand-written taxonomies / demonstrations, we harvest from an optimizer' -- is close to the domain-swap move the track brief explicitly warns is scored as a modest delta. (2) Battle & Gollapudi 2024 on eccentric automatic prompts established that optimizer-discovered text is idiosyncratic and does not carry, which pre-empts part of the negative-transfer finding. GEPA/MIPROv2/OPRO/APE genuinely do not attribute gain to prompt parts, so the *object* (clause x target matrix over optimizer output) is new; the *finding* it is designed to produce is largely anticipated, so a reviewer will read a confirmed hypothesis as replication at a new granularity rather than discovery. The proposal's dismissal of SPoT/ATTEMPT is correct and not the problem.
reviews.strongest_objection: The central dissociation is measured with two non-comparable operators, so prediction (b) (Spearman ~0.0-0.3) and prediction (c) (content clauses transfer at delta <= 0) are close to guaranteed by the design rather than by any fact about portability. Experiment (4) estimates source contribution by *deleting* a clause from a co-adapted, jointly optimized prompt; experiment (5) estimates cross-task contribution by *appending* that same clause into a foreign prompt in a fixed slot. Deletion from a coherent optimized whole is superadditive -- removing a task-specific content clause can break references that other clauses depend on -- while a single appended sentence in a fixed slot is near-inert almost regardless of content. A low correlation between a deletion delta and an insertion delta is the expected result even if clause portability is perfectly predicted by source contribution, and the attenuation correction in experiment (6) does not touch this: it corrects for unreliability, not for the fact that the two quantities are different estimands. Consequently the paper's headline claim ('optimizers discover two kinds of text') is confounded with 'deleting differs from appending', and the mixed-model DeltaR^2 >= 0.15 for clause type is equally exposed, since clause type is strongly correlated with how self-contained a clause is and therefore with how much it survives being ripped out of context. A related, smaller instance of the same problem: the sham control in arm (5) is a semantically inverted clause, which for an output-contract clause ('always emit JSON' -> 'never emit JSON') is actively destructive against a format-sensitive parser rather than neutral, so the sham baseline is biased in exactly the direction that flatters the proposal's favored clause type.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Add a symmetric arm: insert each clause into its OWN task's baseline prompt, in the same fixed slot, on the same attribution set, and define source contribution as that insertion delta. Then the dissociation test in (6) compares insertion-to-insertion, and any residual low correlation is about portability rather than about operator. Keep the leave-one-clause-out numbers as a secondary, explicitly non-comparable measure of co-adaptation. Second, pre-register how prediction (e) is evaluated: 'removing format-compliance-driven items from the metric' is undefined for exact-match GSM8K/BBH/MBPP, and it needs to be a concrete lenient-parse re-scoring rule fixed before the matrix is computed, otherwise the accuracy-vs-contract split is decided after seeing the results. Third, replace the sham control for contract clauses with a neutral-but-plausible contract clause naming a different, unenforced format, so the control is not destructive by construction. Fourth, fit the mixed model with crossed random effects for source task and target task; with 8 tasks the effective n for a type-level claim is closer to 8 than to the 15-40 cells the power calculation assumes, and the quoted 1.2-point detectable effect is optimistic under that clustering.
reviews.missing_baseline: A zero-measurement LLM-authored library: give the frontier reflector model the 7 source-task optimized prompts and ask it to write a generic transferable prefix at the same token cap, with no clause segmentation, no attribution, and no cross-task scoring. This is the direct competitor to the entire ~168k-generation measurement apparatus, and it is strictly stronger than the plan's baseline (iii), which is hand-written *without seeing any optimization run* and therefore does not test whether the expensive causal estimation -- as opposed to merely reading the optimized prompts -- was necessary. If the LLM-summarized prefix matches the measured library, the paper's method reduces to an expensive way to reproduce a one-call summary. Also missing: a multi-source whole-prompt warm start (concatenated or LLM-merged prompts from all 7 sources); baseline (ii) transfers only the single best source prompt, which is the weakest form of the obvious cheap alternative.
reviews.preprint_collision: There is no collision check. The field is empty and the Related Work section states outright that all citations are unverified and the literature-search backend was unavailable, so the submission reports zero searches of any kind, indexed or preprint. Under the standard applied here that is a weakness, not a neutral: novelty is asserted, not established. This matters more than usual because the anchor method, GEPA (Agrawal et al., 2025), is itself a recent preprint, and the highest-risk collision zone is precisely its 2025-2026 follow-up literature -- analyses of what optimized prompts actually contain, ablations of GEPA/MIPRO-returned instructions, and reusable system-prompt/meta-prompt library papers -- none of which the authors have looked at. I cannot name a specific preprint that already makes this claim from the text under review, but the absence of any search means the authors cannot either, and a reviewer who does spend ten minutes on arXiv is likely to surface a component-ablation or transferable-instruction-library paper from the last two quarters. This should be resolved before the novelty claim in the Related Work section ('the new object here is a clause x target portability matrix') can be credited.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A causal clause-by-target portability matrix for GEPA-discovered prompts, used to claim that a clause's value on its source task does not predict its cross-task value while a cheap seven-way clause-type label does, and to assemble a zero-rollout library of high-portability clauses priced in cold-start GEPA rollouts.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Self-Discover (Zhou et al., 2024) already ships a fixed library of domain-general reasoning modules that are selected and composed per task with zero task-specific optimization, which is exactly the artifact and the deployment story of Experiment (7); PromptBreeder (Fernando et al., 2023) likewise carries a reusable pool of domain-general 'thinking styles' and mutation prompts across tasks. Neither is cited. Together they largely pre-empt the loop-closing contribution (a reusable text library of domain-general prompt components beats nothing and costs no rollouts), leaving the genuine delta as the *measurement* — harvesting components from what an optimizer actually found and estimating their transfer causally. On the attribution machinery, prompt-compression and context-attribution work (LLMLingua; ContextCite, Cohen-Wang et al., 2024) already does leave-one-segment-out and regression-based marginals over prompt/context spans, so the estimator is not new either; only its application to optimizer-discovered clauses across tasks is. The proposal's distinction from SPoT/ATTEMPT ('soft prompts have no clause structure') is correct but is the modest-delta move the track brief explicitly warns is scored as a domain swap.
reviews.strongest_objection: The central dissociation is close to definitionally true, so confirming it carries almost no information. Prediction (c) says task-specific-content clauses show mean cross-task delta <= 0: a clause containing HotpotQA entity vocabulary or GSM8K arithmetic scaffolding, appended verbatim into an MBPP prompt, is simply off-topic text, and 'off-topic text does not help and sometimes hurts' is already the settled finding of the prompt-sensitivity literature the proposal itself cites. Nothing in the design isolates whether clause *type* predicts transfer over and above plain topical relevance: the mixed model in (6) controls for source contribution and clause length but not for any measure of clause-to-target semantic relevance, and the domain-scrubbed condition — the one manipulation that could separate 'type' from 'topicality' — is demoted to an ablation rather than being the primary contrast. Strip that away and the paper's one non-trivial claim is (d), the rollout equivalence, and that number is the most fragile quantity in the design: it is obtained by inverting a cold-start budget curve sampled at 0/10/25/50/100/300 with a measured per-run SD of ~3 points, so the 10-50 rollout region of the curve is flat within the proposal's own noise floor. If cold-start GEPA at 25 rollouts is not separable from 0 rollouts, then 'the library is worth 25-75 rollouts' is a statement about an interval of the curve where nothing is measurable, and the bootstrap CI on the inverse map will plausibly run from 0 to the whole budget. The proposal predicts a CI excluding zero and also predicts a low Spearman correlation, i.e. it stakes its headline on a null it is underpowered to distinguish from noise and a point estimate it is underpowered to bound. A secondary but real hole: split-half reliability across GEPA seeds is the linchpin of the attenuation correction, yet different seeds return different prompts with different clause sets, so it is unclear which clauses even have two measurements to correlate — beyond the near-duplicate-merged subset, the reliability estimate is undefined and the attenuation correction unfalsifiable.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Three changes. (1) Make relevance, not type, the thing type must beat: add clause-to-target semantic similarity (and the domain-scrubbed variant of every clause) as primary conditions rather than ablations, and require the mixed model's DeltaR^2 >= 0.15 to survive after relevance is entered as a covariate — that turns a tautology into a real test of the 'two kinds of text' theory. (2) Drop rollout equivalence as the headline and replace it with a pre-registered fixed-budget contrast the design can actually resolve: library-seeded GEPA versus cold-start GEPA at 25 and 50 rollouts, paired per target, with the target count raised from 8 to at least 16 clusters so the leave-one-target-out claim has more than eight independent generalization units (the '24 paired observations' figure treats three seeds within a fold as independent, which they are not; the effective n for a cross-domain claim is 8, and the stated ~1.5-point sensitivity is correspondingly optimistic). (3) Add the LLM-distillation baseline below, and actually run the preprint search. Also trim: the ablation list (position x3, granularity x3, single-type libraries, 1-vs-7 sources, second executor, plus a full library-as-seed budget curve) multiplies the ~330k headline generations several-fold and does not fit the stated one-node, few-hundred-dollar ceiling as written.
reviews.missing_baseline: A zero-rollout, zero-measurement LLM-distilled prefix: hand the reflector model the seven source-task optimized prompts and ask it to write a generic, domain-general prefix of matched token length. This is the baseline that prices the paper's entire expensive apparatus — the ~168k-generation clause x target matrix exists only to rank clauses by measured portability, and if a single frontier-model call over the same source prompts produces a prefix that matches the harvested library on held-out targets, then the causal portability estimation bought nothing and the contribution collapses to the attribution study alone. The plan has a human checklist written blind (iii) and whole-prompt warm start (ii), but neither tests this: (iii) never sees the optimizer output, and (ii) transfers one prompt whole. Secondarily missing, and specifically named in the track brief: a task-similarity retrieval baseline in the SPoT/ATTEMPT spirit — pick the single nearest source task by embedding and reuse its prompt — which is the standard cheap way to get cross-task transfer and which the proposal cites as related work without implementing.
reviews.preprint_collision: The Preprint Collision Check field is empty, and the Related Work section states outright that all citations are unverified because the literature-search backend was unavailable. By the standard applied here that is a substantive weakness, not a neutral: the proposal asserts that no prior work attributes optimizer gain to parts of the returned prompt or measures those parts' portability, and it has run zero searches to support that assertion. The claim is also implausible on its face for a 2025-2026 submission — prompt-component attribution, prompt compression by span importance, and reusable domain-general instruction libraries are all active arXiv areas, and GEPA itself (cited as 2025) is recent enough that follow-up analyses of what its returned prompts contain are exactly the kind of preprint that would appear within months. At minimum the authors must search for and address: recent work decomposing or ablating optimizer-produced prompts; Self-Discover-style and PromptBreeder-style reusable domain-general component libraries; Shapley/leave-one-out attribution over prompt spans; and any cross-task prompt-component transfer study posted since GEPA. Until that search exists, novelty here is asserted rather than established, and I have scored it accordingly.
